annotations.title: From what a person wants to the specs that do it

description: From what a person wants to the specs that do it, when no single part does it all or the wants pull against each other. Each want is a requirement naming its route (the key of the lottery, item, grant, farm or contest it is about; its family follows from that): a draw ("pay-in" {currencies: [{token, amount}]}, "burn", "refund-as-paid", "free-entry" {grant, perPerson, spendable}, "one-approval", "one-draw", "one-token", "first-reward-no-sol"); a sale of an item ("pay-in", "fixed-price", "instant", "fair-scarce" {perPerson, list}, "one-approval"); a reward, a grant ("per-person" {claims}, "no-server", "bot-proof", "bounded" {total}, "first-reward-no-sol"; a server’s voucher keys as "serverKeys" on any of them); staking, a farm ("emission-cap" {total}, "predictable", "no-lock", "whale-fair"; "perDay" and "days" on any of them); a contest ("no-owner-trust", "equal-stakes" {amount}, "refund-if-no-result"; decider keys as "serverKeys"). Takes the spec as it stands, with each route’s skeleton. For each route it builds every combination of known bridges (an entry token each currency buys, crafted in the purchase; a payment held to the draw; a fixed-price listing in each currency; an allowlist; a deciding voucher server; a fixed or shared rate, minted or from a vault, with an end or a halving; a decider key), checks each, tests every requirement on it, and answers the designs best first (what the person asked for, then how it plays, then how clean, then how secure), with what each keeps (✓), keeps in part (~) and gives up (✗), a sentence for the person and what each needs from them; when none keeps them all, what has to give. Each design’s spec is in `designs`.
